literal: Those who lack kind consideration are without eyes; those who possess eyes, even the absence of kind consideration is not there for them.
translation: Those who lack kind consideration have no eyes; for those who truly possess eyes, the absence of kind consideration is impossible.
modern: கண்ணோட்டம் இல்லாதவர்கள் கண் இல்லாதவர்கள் ஆவர்; கண் உடையவர்கள் என்பவர்களிடம் கண்ணோட்டம் இல்லாமல் இருப்பது இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet defines what true eyes are by linking them to the quality of 'kaṇṇōṭṭam' (kind consideration or benignity). The author states that those who do not show kind consideration to others are effectively blind, lacking real eyes. Conversely, those who are said to possess eyes will never be without this quality of kind consideration. The play on the word 'kaṇ' (eye) and 'kaṇṇōṭṭam' (the flow of the eye, i.e., kindness) emphasizes that the physical organ is useless without its corresponding moral virtue.
